Two games I came across recently that are good two player games are Love Letter and Guillotine.

Guillotine is a game in revolutionary France, where you are Guillotine operators trying to behead the most valuable royalty and military figures. During your turn, you can play one card to change the lineup of "victims", then behead the one at the front of the line. After three "days" (full lines of victims) points are counted up, and a winner is declared.

Love Letter is a quick game that I can't simply explain, so I will direct you to this video from TableTop. Watch that, and enjoy, since it will describe much better than I will without playing it with you. Just know that it plays well two players as well.
We actually play Love Letter fairly often, we recently also got the Batman version :)

If she likes deck builders try Dominion. It's hands-down the best deck building game available imo and it has tons of expansions to customize the game. ~$40

Another one I like is Carcassone, it's a tile-laying game and it also has some good expansions.

Good thing about Dominion is you don't have to start with the original. The expansions can be played as stand a lone game.

I second Dominion. My husband and I have all the expansions and it's easily our most played games.

And you can buy the base cards as their own set for like $10 on amazon now. It makes transporting the game so much easier as well.

Khet and Trench are cool. I think that there is a real lack of 2 player focused games right now, in favor of party style games (which I also love, don't get me wrong). These games can often be run 2 player but with varying degrees of success. I'm a big fan of classics 2 players like backgammon, chess, and go and it's hard to find modern games in the same vein.
